title: Overlap and Pause
description: A three-person release check-in written to exercise speech overlap honestly. It contains two genuine backchannel overlaps (a listener says a short word while another participant is mid-sentence), one genuine interruption where the floor changes hands, and several sentence-final words followed by long silences. The long silences are the point: a decoder that stretches a word's end through the following pause turns a clean gap into a fabricated overlap with whoever speaks next, so this fixture distinguishes real simultaneous speech from invented simultaneous speech.

turns.speaker: ana
turns.text: Let me walk through where the release actually stands today. The installer is finished and the documentation has already been merged.
turns.note: long turn; ends into a deliberate four second silence

turns.speaker: ben
turns.note: GENUINE OVERLAP: backchannel while ana is mid-sentence

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: Okay, so what is actually left before we can ship it?
turns.note: starts after a long gap; ana's final word must not stretch into this turn

turns.speaker: ana
turns.note: short turn followed by another long silence

turns.speaker: cara
turns.text: I can take that one. I will write it this afternoon and post the link in the channel well before the standup tomorrow.
turns.note: long turn that a backchannel lands inside

turns.speaker: ana
turns.note: GENUINE OVERLAP: backchannel while cara is mid-sentence

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: Wait, does that block the announcement?
turns.note: GENUINE OVERLAP: real interruption, the floor changes hands

turns.speaker: cara
turns.text: No, the announcement goes out separately.

turns.speaker: ana
turns.note: final turn; trailing silence to the end of the meeting
